function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
The debate over the “greatest basketball player ever” is one of the most lively and enduring conversations in sports, and it’s hard to give a definitive answer because it depends on what criteria you value most. Below is a balanced look at the most frequently cited candidates, the arguments in their favor, and some of the counter‑arguments that keep the discussion alive.

| Player | Era | Key Achievements | Strengths | Why Some Call Them the GOAT |
|--------|-----|------------------|-----------|-----------------------------|
| **Michael Jordan** | 1980s‑1990s | 6× NBA champion, 5× MVP, 14× All‑Star, 10× scoring champion, 6× Finals MVP | Scoring, clutch play, defensive tenacity, global brand | Dominated the NBA during the 1990s, won two three‑peats, unmatched competitiveness, transcended the sport globally. |
| **LeBron James** | 2000s‑present | 4× NBA champion, 4× MVP, 19× All‑Star (as of 2024), 2× Olympic gold, 3× Finals MVP | Versatility, longevity, playmaking, physical prime, adaptability to different teams | Sustained elite performance across multiple eras, consistently leads teams deep into playoffs, demonstrates all‑around excellence. |
| **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** | 1970s‑1980s | 6× NBA champion, 6× MVP, 19× All‑Star, 19× All‑Defensive, 38,387 career points (all‑time leader until 2023) | Skyhook, longevity, consistency, defensive presence | Holds the all‑time scoring record, dominated for 20+ seasons, won championships with two franchises. |
| **Bill Russell** | 1950s‑1960s | 11× NBA champion, 5× MVP, 12× All‑Star, 12× All‑Defensive | Defensive dominance, leadership, championship pedigree | 11 championships in 13 seasons, built the Celtics dynasty, unmatched playoff success. |
| **Magic Johnson** | 1980s | 5× NBA champion, 3× MVP, 12× All‑Star, 3× Finals MVP | Playmaking, versatility, leadership | Revolutionized the point‑forward role, led Lakers to multiple championships, iconic rivalry with Larry Bird. |
| **Larry Bird** | 1980s | 3× NBA champion, 3× MVP, 12× All‑Star, 3× Finals MVP | Shooting, basketball IQ, competitiveness | Built the Celtics dynasty, legendary rivalry with Magic, clutch performances. |

### Common Criteria Used in the Debate

1. **Championships & Finals Success** – Winning titles is often the most tangible measure. Jordan’s 6 titles and LeBron’s 4 (plus 2 more in 2024) are frequently cited.
2. **Individual Accolades** – MVPs, scoring titles, All‑Star selections, and defensive honors show sustained excellence.
3. **Statistical Dominance** – Points per game, efficiency ratings, and all‑time totals (e.g., Kareem’s scoring record) illustrate impact.
4. **Versatility & Longevity** – Ability to adapt to different teams, eras, and roles (LeBron’s longevity, Russell’s defensive mastery).
5. **Cultural Impact** – Influence on the sport, marketability, and global reach (Jordan’s brand, LeBron’s activism).
6. **Clutch Performance** – Game‑winning plays, playoff heroics, and Finals performances.

3. **Personal Preference** – Many fans choose based on the era they grew up in or the style of play they enjoy.
